data.text: Subscriptions let clients receive real-time updates when data changes. Hot Chocolate uses WebSockets to push events to subscribed clients.
A subscription resolver returns an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`. Hot Chocolate yields values over the WebSocket connection whenever a new event occurs.

data.caption: Subscription flow from server to client.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    participant Database
    Client->>Server: subscription { bookAdded }
    Server-->>Client: WebSocket connection established
    Database-->>Server: New book inserted
    Server-->>Client: Push bookAdded event
    Client->>Client: Update UI

data.text: Create a `Subscription` class and use `[Subscription]` on methods that return `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`.

data.title: Subscription Type
data.content: Notify clients when a new book is added.

data.text: Use `ITopicEventReceiver` to publish events from anywhere in your app — controllers, services, or even hosted services.

data.title: Publishing Events
data.content: Publish a book-added event from a mutation or service.

data.title: WebSocket Transport
data.text: Hot Chocolate uses WebSockets for subscriptions by default. Make sure your reverse proxy or hosting environment supports WebSocket upgrades.

terms.definition: A long-lived GraphQL operation that receives pushed events from the server.
